title: Structured concurrency: scope, job and cancellation

videos.script: A coroutine that nobody is waiting for is a coroutine somebody will forget. It keeps running after the screen has closed, saves half a session, or fails where nobody hears. {{scope}} This lesson is about the rule that stops that. Every coroutine lives in a scope, and the scope waits for all of its children. {{tree}} The children form a tree. Cancellation travels down it. Failure travels up it. {{cancel}} You will see that cancelling is cooperative: a coroutine stops at its next suspension point, and a busy loop that never suspends ignores you completely. {{failure}} Then a refresh where one part fails, and its siblings are cancelled, because the result they were building no longer exists. {{supervisor}} A supervisor scope, for jobs that fail alone. {{timeout}} Timeouts. {{pitfalls}} And two ways to break all of it: a catch that swallows cancellation, and a global scope that waits for nothing.
